plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE with effect-size thresholding
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 121 columns — gene symbol column plus 120 samples) with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 60 cases vs 60 controls, whole blood, human, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two halves — which genes differ, and which differences are large enough to matter — so the plan separates statistical significance from effect size and does not let the first stand in for the second.

Method choice is driven by the cohort size. With 60 per group this is a population-scale cohort, where the negative-binomial count models (DESeq2, edgeR) are documented to exaggerate false positives on human population samples, even under permuted labels (Li et al. 2022). The differential test is therefore limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model on TMM-normalized, filterByExpr-filtered counts, and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test on the same log-CPM matrix runs beside it as a distribution-free control; the report gives the overlap between the two calls, which is the honest measure of how much the parametric assumption is doing.

The 'large enough to matter' half is handled inside the model rather than by a post-hoc fold-change filter: TREAT tests each gene against a stated |log2FC| threshold of 1 (2-fold), which is the only way to get FDR control for the threshold question. The plain (threshold-zero) moderated t-test is reported alongside so the number of significant-but-tiny effects is visible — at n=60 per group the test has power to call biologically trivial shifts, and that gap is the point of the question. Confidence intervals accompany every fold change, and the gene table is sorted by effect size within the significant set.

QC comes first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) because a mislabeled or outlying sample among 120 changes every downstream number and the profile flags no quality concerns that were pre-screened. Enrichment runs on the limma fit itself: camera, which estimates and corrects for inter-gene correlation from the many samples, against MSigDB human hallmark (confirmed staged, 2026.1), plus fgsea preranked on the moderated t-statistic of the same fit — the stated choice for the disputed ranking metric, since a t-statistic scales effect by uncertainty whereas an unshrunken fold change does not. GO BP/CC/MF (staged) serves as the follow-up collection; Reactome C2 is not staged and the step should say so rather than substitute. The final step assembles the report with fit diagnostics, leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record.

One caveat carried through the whole plan: 'case' and 'control' are the only labels the metadata supplies. No disease, no covariates (age, sex, cell composition) are available, and whole blood is dominated by cell-type composition shifts. Any DE signal here is confounded with differential blood cell proportions and cannot be separated from it with the data at hand; the report must state this rather than interpret gene-level changes as cell-intrinsic regulation.

Three counts reported side by side: ordinary moderated-t significant, naive padj+|log2FC|>1 filter, TREAT significant — with the statement that only TREAT controls FDR for the threshold question
Distribution of |log2FC| among ordinary-significant genes summarized (median, quartiles, fraction below 0.5)
Per-gene Wilcoxon rank-sum test with BH adjustment on the voom log-CPM matrix, with overlap versus limma calls reported as a contingency table
Volcano plot distinguishing TREAT-significant genes from ordinary-significant genes
Gene tables saved sorted by effect size within the significant set
constraints: The fold-change threshold must be tested inside the model with treat(); a post-hoc |log2FC| filter may be reported for comparison only and must be labeled as lacking FDR control
Use lfc = 1 (2-fold) as the stated threshold and name it in every output; if the analyst wants a different threshold, it must be stated, not chosen after seeing the results
Wilcoxon runs on the same filtered gene set and the same voom log-CPM values, not on raw counts
Select genes by adjusted p-value, never by raw p-value or fold change alone
caveats: A threshold of 2-fold is a stated convention, not a biologically derived cutoff for whole blood — say so; whole-blood case/control differences are often genuinely small and a near-empty TREAT list is a real result, not a failure
If limma and Wilcoxon disagree substantially, the parametric assumption is doing heavy lifting and the limma-only calls should be presented with reduced confidence
Do not interpret the direction of any gene without the condition labels stated explicitly

steps.name: Hallmark and GO enrichment on the limma fit
steps.question: Which biological processes are coordinately shifted between the 60 cases and 60 controls in whole blood, on the full ranked gene list rather than a thresholded subset?
steps.description: Two complementary enrichment passes on the T1S2 limma fit. (1) camera on the fit against the human MSigDB hallmark collection — camera estimates the inter-gene correlation of each set from the 120 samples and corrects the set test for it, which matters at this cohort size. (2) fgsea preranked on the full list of tested genes ranked by the moderated t-statistic of the same fit — the stated choice for the disputed ranking metric, because a t-statistic scales the effect by its uncertainty while an unshrunken fold change does not, and signed p-values tie at the top. Restrict sets to 15-500 genes after intersecting with the tested genes. The universe is the tested (filterByExpr-surviving) genes, never the whole genome. Run the same two passes against the human GO biological-process sets as the follow-up collection. Collapse overlapping significant sets and report one representative per group, with the full table as a supplement. Report the leading-edge genes of each significant fgsea set with their moderated t-statistics, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Report the fraction of tested gene symbols that failed to match any set. Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations.
steps.context: Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets and human GO gene sets, both keyed on HGNC symbols — the count matrix's first column is already gene symbols, so no ID conversion is strictly required; if a conversion to Entrez is performed, report the unmapped share and never mix identifier spaces between the list and the universe. Both collections were present in this environment at plan time (MSigDB 2026.1 hallmark and GO BP/CC/MF, human, symbol GMTs); resolve them at run time rather than assuming a path. A curated Reactome pathway collection is NOT staged in this environment — if it is absent at run time, say so in the output and use GO as the second collection instead of substituting a different resource silently. No KEGG collection is served.
acceptance_criteria: camera results against human hallmark sets, with the estimated inter-gene correlation reported per set
fgsea preranked results on the moderated t-statistic against human hallmark, with NES, BH-adjusted p, set size and leading-edge genes
Both passes repeated against human GO biological-process sets
Gene set size window of 15-500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes, and reported
Universe stated as the tested genes, with the count
Redundant significant sets collapsed to representatives, full table retained as a supplement
Collection name and version, the ranking metric (moderated t), and the fgsea seed all recorded
Share of tested genes not matching any gene set reported
constraints: Rank by the moderated t-statistic from the limma fit — this is the stated choice among the disputed metrics; do not rank by unshrunken log2FC alone or by a signed p-value
Give fgsea the FULL ranked list of tested genes; never cut the list at an adjusted p-value or fold change first
Universe = genes that survived filterByExpr and were tested, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
Set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes
Use human gene sets only — the data is Homo sapiens whole blood
Do not run an over-representation test on the significant-gene list if fewer than ~50 genes pass; use the ranked method and state the list size
Resolve the gene set collections from the environment's reference store at run time; report the exact collection version used
caveats: Enrichment results depend strongly on method — camera and fgsea will not agree fully; report the overlap and the disagreement, and present each set as a hypothesis, not a finding
GO sets are hierarchically nested, so significant parents and children are one finding, not many — collapse before counting

In whole blood, an immune or cell-type gene set surfacing may reflect a shift in leukocyte proportions rather than transcriptional regulation within a cell type; state this alternative explanation explicitly
Reactome C2 is not staged in this environment; if it remains absent, report the gap rather than substituting

grounding.reason: R-0088: at >=50 per group the enrichment runs on the limma-voom fit with camera plus fgsea on the moderated t; for the disputed R-0108 metric the plan chooses the moderated t-statistic (uncertainty-scaled, no p-value ties). R-0098 asks Reactome as the second collection but it is not staged here, so GO (staged) is the follow-up and the gap is reported.

steps.name: Consolidated report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes differ between the 60 cases and 60 controls, and which differences are large enough to matter', with all methods, thresholds and limitations stated?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Lead with the two counts that answer the question: genes significant at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 from the limma-voom moderated t-test, and genes passing TREAT at |log2FC| > 1 — the latter being the answer to 'large enough to matter'. Give the gene table with log2FC, its 95% confidence interval, standard error, average expression, moderated t, raw p and adjusted p, sorted by effect size within the significant set. Carry the fit diagnostics before the tables: the voom mean-variance trend and the MA/mean-difference plot (these take the role of DESeq2's MA and dispersion plots for a limma fit), plus the raw p-value histogram. Report the design formula (~ condition), the reference level, the contrast direction, the filter, the number of genes tested out of 12,000, and the number of DE genes. Report the Wilcoxon concordance from T1S3 as the control on the parametric test. For the enrichment, state the collection and its version, the ranking metric (moderated t), the universe, the size window, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, and note that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with a limitations section and a full reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the fgsea seed, and the gene set collection versions.
steps.context: The audience needs to distinguish what the data supports from what it does not. Two limitations must be stated prominently and not buried: (1) the metadata carries only a case/control label — no disease name, no age, sex, or blood cell composition — so nothing can be adjusted for and the DE signal is confounded with leukocyte proportion differences that are the dominant source of whole-blood expression variation; (2) limma-voom at 60 per group holds the FDR closer to nominal than count models but is not guaranteed to hold it, which is why the Wilcoxon control is reported beside it.
acceptance_criteria: Report leads with the number of significant genes and, separately, the number passing the 2-fold TREAT threshold
Gene table carries log2FC, 95% CI, standard error, AveExpr, moderated t, raw and adjusted p, sorted by effect size within the significant set
voom mean-variance plot, MA plot and p-value histogram appear before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
Design, reference level, contrast direction, filter, n tested (of 12,000), n DE, and all thresholds stated
Wilcoxon-vs-limma concordance reported as the control on the parametric test
Enrichment section states collection + version, ranking metric, universe, size window, leading-edge genes, and the method-dependence caveat
Limitations section explicitly names the cell-composition confound and the absence of any covariate beyond condition
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed, and collection versions stored with the results
constraints: Report effect size beside every p-value; never present a ranked gene list ordered by p-value alone
State the limma-voom FDR caution (doi:10.1186/s13059-022-02648-4) explicitly in the methods narrative
Do not claim a biological mechanism or a disease interpretation — the metadata names no disease
If the TREAT list is empty or near-empty, report that as the finding rather than lowering the threshold to produce a list
caveats: Whole blood: gene-level differences cannot be separated from differential leukocyte composition with these inputs; no deconvolution covariate is available and adding one post-hoc would be an unvalidated adjustment
A large significant-gene count with small fold changes is the expected shape at n=60 per group and should be presented as such, not as a strong biological signal

grounding.reason: R-0089 and R-0085 require effect size and its uncertainty beside every p-value with sorting by effect size; R-0087 the fit diagnostics (voom mean-variance and MD plot for a limma fit); R-0041/R-0051/R-0086 the method, threshold, collection and reproducibility record.
